[10], from Jónsson [5]), the claim that the results rest on an analogue of the derived-space and Cantor-Bendixson analysis (with p. 515 and p. 522: Theorem 2.8 is a Cantor-Bendixson analogue with a similar proof), and n. 1 (the paper is, up to minor emendations, the 1962 Chicago dissertation); (2) p. 516: the attribution to Vaught [16] and Łoś [9] of completeness of κ-categorical theories without finite models (route lines 56-62 give the argument without it); (3) p. 518: the basis of S(A) has power equal to κ(A) modulo ℵ0 (route lines 85-86 state only the upper bound); (4) p. 520: Definition 2.2 and many following results and proofs remain valid in many other categories of continuous onto maps between compact spaces, and n. 12 (the terms algebraic and transcendental are suggested by Example I and related to Jónsson's generalized algebraic extensions [6]); (5) p. 521 n. 13: the variant of Definition 2.2(2) with 'a single point' in place of 'set of isolated points', combining rank and degree into one rank; (6) p. 523: the sufficient automorphism condition for a consistent Q ⊆ F(A) to lie in a unique point of S(A), with its proof, and n. 14 (the weakened condition, an automorphism of some model C ⊇ B, is also necessary; cf. 17]; Theorem 5.2 for κ = κ^ℵ0 proved in [10] without total transcendence, and the example of a theory that is not totally transcendental and a κ > ℵ0 with κ^ℵ0 ≠ κ having no countably saturated model of power κ;
